# rocelet register map

*Generated by `regs/rocelet_regs.py` (version 0.3.0); do not edit by hand.*

One AXI4-Lite slave (`s_axil_*`), 32-bit data, byte addresses, 64 KB window (offsets below
0x400 are decoded, the rest read 0). It runs in the engine clock (`clk`, the MAC user clock):
put a clock converter in front of it when the CPU is in another domain. Writes take effect
in the clock after the write response; reads are answered in a fixed number of clocks.
Unused bits read 0 and should be written 0.

Access: **RO** read only; **RW** read/write; **W1** a write performs an action (reads return 0).

## Configuration model

- Global registers (MAC, IP, timers) are written once after reset, before any QP is committed.
- A QP is configured by writing the `QP_*` staging registers and then `QP_COMMIT`. The commit
  writes every per-QP table of the engine for `QP_INDEX` in one step and resets all of the
  QP's state (PSNs, retry counters, error state, READ resources). Commit only a QP that has no
  outstanding work requests (`WR_OUTSTANDING` = 0, or after `QP_ERR_CMD` flushed them).
- Memory windows are written the same way (`MR_*`, then `MR_COMMIT`). Window *i* serves the
  R_Keys whose low log2(NUM_MR) bits equal *i*; the full 32-bit key is compared.
- The QP-error flow: an error stops the QP (requester: further work requests complete with
  status FLUSHED; responder: requests are dropped), sets its bit in `QP_ERR_MAP*`, latches
  `LAST_REQ_ERR` / `LAST_RESP_ERR` and `STATUS.ERR` (and `irq` when `CTRL.IRQ_EN`). Recover by
  exchanging new parameters with the host and committing the QP again.

| 0x048 | RNR_MIN | RW | 0xA | Floor of the RNR wait decoded from a received RNR NAK, microseconds (20 bits). |

| 0x054 | ACKREQ_N | RW | 0x10 | Requester: AckReq every N packets inside a message (0 = only on the last packet of each message). |

| 0x064 | RETRY | RW | 0x77 | Requester retry limits (as the IBTA retry_cnt / rnr_retry). |
| 0x068 | PACE_RATE | RW | 0x0 | Requester rate limit (token bucket over all QPs): credit added per clock, in 1/256 byte (wire bytes: payload + 98). 0 = no limit. INC = rate [b/s] / 8 / f_clk [Hz] x 256: 100 Gb/s at 322.27 MHz = 9930, 50 Gb/s = 4965; 40 Gb/s at 156.25 MHz = 8192, 10 Gb/s = 2048. |
| 0x06C | PACE_BURST | RW | 0x4000 | Requester rate limit: bucket size in bytes (the largest burst at line rate). |
| 0x070 | LINK_GRACE | RW | 0x1E8480 | Requester: timer ticks (microseconds at the default TICK_DIV; 24 bits, max 16.7 s) after link_up rises during which the ACK timeouts stay held, for a link partner whose port is up before it answers. With link_up = aligned & no local / remote fault the grace starts at the partner's own link-up (see docs/host-setup.md, link flaps). Reset 2,000,000 = 2 s. 0 = no grace. While link_up is low the ACK timeouts are held anyway; an ACK that became overdue meanwhile times out at once when the hold ends. |
| 0x074 | PAUSE_QCLK | RW | - | Length of one received 802.3x PAUSE quantum (512 bit times) in engine clocks x 256, for the quanta a MAC reports with mac_pause_valid / mac_pause_quanta (since 0.3.0; 0.2.x used the 100G value at any speed). Reset value ceil(131072 x CLK_KHZ / (LINK_GBPS x 10^6)): 423 at 100G / 322.27 MHz, 512 at 40G / 156.25 MHz, 2048 at 10G / 156.25 MHz. Firmware rewrites it when one bitstream runs the link at another speed. |

### 0x020 CTRL

| Bits | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [0] | RESET | hold the engine and the MAC glue in reset (register values are kept). Reset value 0 |
| [1] | RX_EN | accept frames from the MAC. Reset value 1 |
| [2] | TX_EN | start frames towards the MAC. Reset value 1 |
| [3] | READ_CONT | answer a partial duplicate READ as a continuation (MIDDLE/LAST) of the original response instead of a new FIRST/ONLY response. Reset value READ_CONT_DEFAULT |
| [4] | LOSS_FATAL | requester: a NAK-sequence or a timeout puts the QP into the error state instead of recovering. Reset value 0 |
| [5] | VLAN_RX_STRIP | remove 802.1Q VID-0 priority tags on receive. Reset value 1 |
| [6] | VLAN_TX_TAG | tag every RoCE frame sent with VLAN_TCI. Reset value 0 |
| [7] | ARP_INT | answer ARP requests and ICMP echo requests internally (else they go to the other-traffic port). Reset value 1 |
| [8] | OTHER_RX_EN | forward frames that are not RoCE (and not handled internally) to the other-traffic port; 0 = drop them. Reset value 0 |
| [9] | PAUSE_RX_EN | honour received 802.3x PAUSE frames (no new frame starts while paused). Reset value 1 |
| [10] | PAUSE_RX_LEVEL | also hold TX while the MAC holds mac_pause_hold (a MAC that times the received quanta itself, e.g. omac; the CMAC's stat_rx_pause_req[8]). Reset value 0 |
| [11] | PAUSE_TX_EN | request 802.3x PAUSE (mac_pause_req) from the RX FIFO level. Reset value 1 |
| [12] | IRQ_EN | drive irq while a QP error is latched (STATUS.ERR). Reset value 1 |

### 0x024 STATUS

| Bits | Field | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [0] | IN_RESET | engine held in reset |
| [1] | MAC_RX_STATUS | mac_rx_status input (the MAC's RX is aligned / block-locked; MAC_ALIGNED before 0.3.0) |
| [2] | PAUSE_GATE | TX held by a received PAUSE |
| [3] | PAUSE_REQ | PAUSE requested from the MAC (mac_pause_req) |
| [4] | ERR | a QP error is latched (see QP_ERR_MAP, LAST_REQ_ERR, LAST_RESP_ERR); cleared by CMD.CLR_ERR |
| [5] | LINK_UP | link_up input (synchronised) |
| [6] | TIMER_HOLD | requester ACK timeouts held: link_up low, or LINK_GRACE running after it rose (only once link_up has been seen high since reset) |

|---|---|---|
| [15:0] | QUANTA | quanta of the last received PAUSE |
| [16] | GATE |  |
| [17] | REQ |  |

## Counters

32-bit, wrapping, at 0x200 + 4 x index; `CMD.CLR_COUNTERS` clears them. Built when
`COUNTERS_EN` = 1 (otherwise they read 0). 64-bit counters at 0x300: read `_LO` first,
which latches `_HI`.

| Index | Offset | Name | Counts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0x200 | CNT_RX_FRAMES | frames received from the MAC (each tlast) |
| 1 | 0x204 | CNT_RX_FCS_ERR | frames the MAC flagged bad (tuser), dropped |
| 2 | 0x208 | CNT_RX_FIFO_DROP | frames dropped by the RX FIFO (full, oversize, reset) |
| 3 | 0x20C | CNT_RX_ROCE | frames to the engine (UDP port 4791) |
| 4 | 0x210 | CNT_RX_ARP | ARP frames |
| 5 | 0x214 | CNT_RX_ICMP | ICMP frames to the local IP |
| 6 | 0x218 | CNT_RX_OTHER | other frames forwarded to the other-traffic port |
| 7 | 0x21C | CNT_RX_OTHER_DROP | other frames dropped (CTRL.OTHER_RX_EN = 0) |
| 8 | 0x220 | CNT_RX_VLAN_STRIP | VID-0 tags removed |
| 9 | 0x224 | CNT_RX_VLAN_OTHER | tagged frames with VID != 0 (not stripped) |
| 10 | 0x228 | CNT_RX_ICRC_BAD | RoCE frames with a bad ICRC (dropped) |
| 11 | 0x22C | CNT_RX_PARSE_DROP | UDP-4791 frames the parser rejected (IP, opcode, TVer, ...) |
| 12 | 0x230 | CNT_RX_CNP | CNPs (opcode 0x81) received and dropped |
| 13 | 0x234 | CNT_RX_ACK | ACKs received (requester) |
| 14 | 0x238 | CNT_RX_NAK_SEQ | NAK PSN-sequence-error received |
| 15 | 0x23C | CNT_RX_RNR_NAK | RNR NAKs received |
| 16 | 0x240 | CNT_RX_NAK_FATAL | NAK invalid request / remote access / remote operational received |
| 17 | 0x244 | CNT_RX_REQ | request packets executed by the responder (new PSN) |
| 18 | 0x248 | CNT_RX_DUP | duplicate request packets (re-ACKed / READ re-executed) |
| 19 | 0x24C | CNT_RX_OOS | out-of-sequence request packets (NAK-seq sent or suppressed) |
| 20 | 0x250 | CNT_RX_QP_DROP | packets for an unknown, unconfigured or failed QP |
| 21 | 0x254 | CNT_RX_READ | READ requests executed (incl. duplicates) |
| 22 | 0x258 | CNT_RX_READ_CONT | duplicate READs answered as a continuation |
| 23 | 0x25C | CNT_RX_RNR_SENT | RNR NAKs sent (send_rnr) |
| 24 | 0x260 | CNT_RX_CPL | receive completions (SEND, WRITE with immediate) |
| 25 | 0x264 | CNT_TX_FRAMES | frames sent to the MAC |
| 26 | 0x268 | CNT_TX_REQ | requester packets sent (incl. retransmissions) |
| 27 | 0x26C | CNT_TX_ACK | ACKs sent |
| 28 | 0x270 | CNT_TX_NAK | NAKs sent (sequence, RNR, fatal) |
| 29 | 0x274 | CNT_TX_READ_RESP | READ response packets sent |
| 30 | 0x278 | CNT_TX_ARP_ICMP | ARP / ICMP replies sent |
| 31 | 0x27C | CNT_TX_OTHER | frames sent from the other-traffic port |
| 32 | 0x280 | CNT_TX_UNDERRUN | clock cycles with tvalid low inside a frame towards the MAC, on the 512-bit side or after the width converter (must stay 0) |
| 33 | 0x284 | CNT_TX_VLAN_TAG | frames tagged |
| 34 | 0x288 | CNT_REQ_WR | work requests accepted |
| 35 | 0x28C | CNT_REQ_WC | work completions emitted |
| 36 | 0x290 | CNT_REQ_WC_ERR | work completions with a non-zero status |
| 37 | 0x294 | CNT_REQ_RTX | retransmission episodes (NAK-sequence, timeout or RNR wait) |
| 38 | 0x298 | CNT_REQ_TIMEOUT | ACK timeouts |
| 39 | 0x29C | CNT_REQ_REX | work requests re-issued by go-back-N |
| 40 | 0x2A0 | CNT_PAUSE_RX | PAUSE frames received (mac_pause_rx_frame) |
| 41 | 0x2A4 | CNT_PAUSE_TX | PAUSE frames sent (mac_pause_tx_frame) |
| 42 | 0x2A8 | CNT_PAUSE_GATE | received PAUSE in force: timer loads (mac_pause_valid), plus rises of mac_pause_hold with CTRL.PAUSE_RX_LEVEL |
| 43 | 0x2AC | CNT_PAUSE_XOFF | PAUSE requests raised (RX FIFO above XOFF) |
| 44 | 0x2B0 | CNT_RSFEC_CORR | FEC corrected codewords (mac_fec_corr_inc; RS-FEC on a 100G CMAC, else 0) |
| 45 | 0x2B4 | CNT_RSFEC_UNCORR | FEC uncorrectable codewords (mac_fec_uncorr_inc) |
| 46 | 0x2B8 | CNT_AXI_WR_ERR | memory writes answered with BRESP != OKAY |
| 47 | 0x2BC | CNT_AXI_RD_ERR | memory read beats answered with RRESP != OKAY |
| 48 | 0x2C0 | CNT_WR_DATA_ERR | work-request payload with tlast not on the last beat of the WR length |
| 49 | 0x2C4 | CNT_LINK_DOWN | link_up falling edges (counted once link_up has been seen high since reset) |
| 64-bit | 0x300 | CYCLES_LO/_HI | clock cycles since CMD.CLR_COUNTERS |
| 64-bit | 0x308 | RX_BYTES_LO/_HI | bytes received from the MAC |
| 64-bit | 0x310 | TX_BYTES_LO/_HI | bytes sent to the MAC |
